edition: Chapter 4 Credit Underwriting as published on KnowVA (article 554400000330850; per-topic change dates in the text)
note: Paraphrased rule records for the VA Golden Loan Path (Chapter 4: income documentation, assets, AUS, Loan Analysis Form 26-6393, residual income and DTI). VA is structurally distinct: residual income is a deterministic guideline test from the Chapter 4 tables, never a conventional DTI test. Anchors must exist in the privately cached official chapter text. Residual income table values are read from the cached text at run time, never typed into code.

rules.text: Income is effective when it is verifiable, stable and reliable, and anticipated to continue for the foreseeable future; only verified income is considered.
rules.anchor: verifiable, stable and reliable, and anticipated to continue for the foreseeable future

rules.text: Verify a minimum of two years of employment; if the present employment is under two years, verify prior employment covering a total of two years or explain why two years could not be verified.
rules.anchor: Verify a minimum of 2 years of employment

rules.text: Employment of less than 12 months is generally not considered stable and reliable unless the facts (training, education, skills related to the position) support a high probability of continued employment, documented on VA Form 26-6393.
rules.anchor: employment less than 12 months is not considered stable and reliable

rules.text: Standard verification is VA Form 26-8497 (or an equivalent format) plus paystub(s) covering the most recent 30-day period with year-to-date information when the employer normally provides paystubs.
rules.anchor: paystub(s) covering the most recent 30-day period with year-to-date information

rules.text: The VOE and paystub(s) must be no more than 120 days old (180 days for new construction) from the closing date; for automatically closed loans within 120 days of the note date.
rules.anchor: must be no more than 120 days old (180 days for new construction)

rules.text: An employment verification service providing the same information as a full Work Number verification may be used; a current paystub is not required with an automated employment verification service.
rules.anchor: A current paystub is not required with an automated employment verification service

rules.text: Assets are verified with VA Form 26-8497a (Request for Verification of Deposit) or electronic or certified copies of the borrower's last two bank statements; verifications no more than 120 days old (180 for new construction).
rules.anchor: certified copies of the borrower’s last two bank statements

rules.text: Approved automated underwriting systems determine a risk classification (terminology such as Approve or Accept) that permits reduced documentation; the systems do not approve or disapprove loans and the underwriter still decides.
rules.anchor: The automated systems do not approve or disapprove loans

rules.text: Documentation guidelines for borrowers not self-employed: employment gaps under 30 days need no explanation on Refer files, under 60 days on Accept/Approve files; current employment is documented by telephone contact plus paystubs covering at least one full month with YTD, bonus and overtime information.
rules.anchor: No explanation for employment gaps is required if the gaps are

rules.text: The underwriter completes VA Form 26-6393, Loan Analysis, with the loan decision in Item 51 and explanations in Item 47 Remarks; the form is not required for IRRRLs except delinquent VA loan refinances.
rules.anchor: Indicate the loan decision in Item 51

rules.text: Item 19: calculate maintenance and utility costs using 14 cents per square foot of gross living area per the appraisal.
rules.anchor: Calculate maintenance and utility costs using 14¢ per square foot

rules.text: Item 32: enter the estimated monthly Federal income tax from IRS tax tables, reduced by an MCC credit when applicable.
rules.anchor: Enter the borrower’s estimated monthly Federal income tax

rules.text: Residual income (balance available for family support, Item 43) is the net income remaining after deduction of debts and obligations and monthly shelter expenses to cover family living expenses; the guideline amounts vary by loan size, family size and region.
rules.anchor: net income remaining (after deduction of debts and obligations and monthly shelter expenses)

rules.text: Table 9 (loan amounts of $79,999 and below) and Table 10 ($80,000 and above) give residual income by family size (1-5) and region (Northeast, Midwest, South, West); for family size over 5 add $75 (Table 9) or $80 (Table 10) per additional member up to a family of seven; Table 11 keys states to regions.
rules.anchor: Table 10: Table of Residual Incomes by Region for Loan Amounts of $80,000 and Above

rules.text: Count all members of the household without regard to the nature of the relationship when determining family size.
rules.anchor: Count all members of the household (without regard to the nature of the relationship)

rules.text: Minimum residual incomes are a guide and should not automatically trigger approval or rejection; inadequate residual income alone can be a basis for disapproval.
rules.anchor: should not automatically trigger approval or rejection of a loan

rules.text: VA's debt-to-income ratio is total monthly debt payments (housing expense, installment debts and other section D obligations) to gross monthly income; it is a guide secondary to residual income.
rules.anchor: ratio of total monthly debt payments (housing expense, installment debts, and other obligations

rules.text: A ratio greater than 41 percent requires close scrutiny; loans closed automatically with a ratio above 41 percent need a statement signed by the underwriter's supervisor justifying approval unless residual income exceeds the guideline by at least 20 percent.
rules.anchor: unless residual income exceeds the guideline by at least 20 percent

rules.text: Tax-free income may be grossed up for the debt-to-income ratio only, using 125 percent of the non-taxable income; actual amounts are not adjusted for residual income.
rules.anchor: Use a figure of 125 percent of the borrower’s non- taxable income

rules.text: Compensating factors may affect the loan decision for marginal residual income or DTI but cannot compensate for unsatisfactory credit; meeting the residual income guideline is not itself a compensating factor.
rules.anchor: They cannot be used to compensate for unsatisfactory credit
